text:
Maya (support): NeptuneLabs reporting ~12-18% 429s from EU-prod since ~22:00 UTC last night. Customer noticed spike after rolling edge SDK v1.2.3 to gateways. Affected customer_id=2643, sample request ids: req_abc123, req_def456. Can we triage?

Jordan (oncall): Looking. Any recent rate-limit config changes in eu-west? or infra deploys?

RateLimitBot: alert: 429_spike detected for customer=2643 region=eu-west-1 window=1m rate=1400rpm threshold=1000rpm

Ethan (eng): Not seeing platform-wide rate-limit changes. Maya, can you paste a raw 429 response (headers + body) and tell us if they see Retry-After / x-rw-* headers? Also need their client concurrency and whether they're using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 multiplexing.

NeptuneOps: We pushed v1.2.3 to all gateways ~21:30 UTC. Each gateway aggregates sensor reads and posts up to 6 small requests/sec during sync bursts. ~300 gateways per region endpoint. We started seeing errors around 22:05. Using HTTP/2 from gateways -> api.redwood.com.

Priya (infra): Infra metrics show per-customer minute-window exceed for 2643 in eu-west-1 — spike matches rollout time. It looks like traffic is concentrated at top-of-minute due to gateway sync alignment (cron-ish). Recommend smoothing client-side first.

Maya (support): Copied example response from their logs:

```
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 17
x-rw-request-id: req_abc123
retry-after: 17
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"rate limit exceeded","code":"rate_limit"}
```

Ethan (eng): Good — headers present. That reset value ~17s implies per-minute sliding window exhausted. Two immediate troubleshooting angles: (1) client behavior — synchronized bursts + no jitter/backoff + high concurrency -> hit minute cap; (2) proxy/multiplexing causing request coalescing at edge.

Jordan (oncall): Short-term mitigation steps we should ask Neptune to try now:
- Honor Retry-After and backoff (exponential + full jitter)
- Reduce concurrency on gateways to 2-3 concurrent requests
- Stagger gateway sync times by random jitter (0-30s)
- If possible, switch small calls to batch endpoint to reduce request count

NeptuneOps: We can push a hotfix to add jitter and lower concurrency. Do you recommend a temp quota bump while we roll?

Priya (infra): We can entertain a temporary soft bump (1.5x) for 12 hours for region eu-west-1 for customer 2643, but need approval from ops and a support ticket with the exact customer id + requested multiplier + justification. We'll monitor error rate.

Ethan (eng): For longer term, items for engineering:
- Add a customer-facing note in docs about "syncing gateways" patterns and recommended jitter/backoff.
- Consider exposing per-customer sliding-window sampling in Console so we can show customers their per-minute peaks.
- Explore a batch ingest endpoint for telemetry-heavy customers.

Maya (support): I'll collect request ids (req_abc123, req_def456, req_ghi789) and ask for client logs (timestamps + gateway id). Also sending a support ticket to ops for temporary bump.

Jordan (oncall): Quick repro steps for eng if needed:
1) Simulate 300 clients, each sending bursts of 6 req/s aligned to top of minute for 5m
2) Use HTTP/2 multiplex to match customer's env
3) Check x-rw-rate-limit-remaining and 429 rates

Ethan (eng): I'll spin up a small repro in staging and run the aligned bursts to validate mitigation (jitter + reduced concurrency). If repro stable, we can add a mitigation doc snippet.

NeptuneOps: Rolling hotfix 1.2.4 to add 0-30s jitter and drop concurrency to 3. ETA ~45m. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maya (support): Status check in 30m after patch and bump request. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
